sanskrit: nārāyaṇaparaṃ satyam ṛtaṃ nārāyaṇātmakam nārāyaṇaparo dharmaḥ punarāvṛttidurlabhaḥ
english: Truth has Nārāyaṇa for its highest ground; the cosmic order is of Nārāyaṇa's very essence. Dharma too is grounded in Nārāyaṇa, that dharma by which return to rebirth is hard to come by.

sanskrit: pravṛttilakṣaṇaś caiva dharmo nārāyaṇātmakaḥ nārāyaṇātmako gandho bhūmau śreṣṭhatamaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: The dharma marked by active engagement in the world is likewise of Nārāyaṇa's essence. Scent itself, the foremost quality residing in earth, is taught to be of Nārāyaṇa's essence.

sanskrit: apāṃ caiva guṇo rājan raso nārāyaṇātmakaḥ jyotiṣāṃ ca guṇo rūpaṃ smṛtaṃ nārāyaṇātmakam
english: And the quality of the waters, O king—taste—is of Nārāyaṇa's essence; the quality of the luminous bodies—form—is taught to be of Nārāyaṇa's essence.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇātmakaś cāpi sparśo vāyuguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ nārāyaṇātmakaś cāpi śabda ākāśasaṃbhavaḥ
english: Touch as well, the quality of wind, is taught to be of Nārāyaṇa's essence; and sound, which arises from space, is likewise of Nārāyaṇa's essence.

sanskrit: manaś cāpi tato bhūtam avyaktaguṇalakṣaṇam nārāyaṇaparaḥ kālo jyotiṣām ayanaṃ ca yat
english: And mind too, which has come to be from that, marked by the quality of the Unmanifest—time has Nārāyaṇa for its highest ground, as does the course of the heavenly lights.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇaparā kīrtiḥ śrīś ca lakṣmīś ca devatāḥ nārāyaṇaparaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ yogo nārāyaṇātmakaḥ
english: Fame has Nārāyaṇa for its highest ground, and the goddesses Śrī and Lakṣmī. Sāṃkhya has Nārāyaṇa for its highest ground, and Yoga is of Nārāyaṇa's essence.

sanskrit: kāraṇaṃ puruṣo yeṣāṃ pradhānaṃ cāpi kāraṇam svabhāvaś caiva karmāṇi daivaṃ yeṣāṃ ca kāraṇam
english: For those who hold the Puruṣa to be the cause, and likewise the primordial Nature as cause, and inherent disposition, and deeds, and fate as cause—

sanskrit: pañcakāraṇasaṃkhyāto niṣṭhā sarvatra vai hariḥ tattvaṃ jijñāsamānānāṃ hetubhiḥ sarvatomukhaiḥ
english: reckoned by these five causes, Hari is verily the final ground in every case—for those who seek to know the truth through reasonings that face in every direction.

sanskrit: tattvam eko mahāyogī harir nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ sabrahmakānāṃ lokānām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca mahātmanām
english: The one Reality is the great yogin, Hari Nārāyaṇa, the Lord—of the worlds together with Brahmā, and of the great-souled seers,

sanskrit: sāṃkhyānāṃ yogināṃ cāpi yatīnām ātmavedinām manīṣitaṃ vijānāti keśavo na tu tasya te
english: of the followers of Sāṃkhya and the yogins, and of the ascetics who know the Self—the inmost thought of all these Keśava knows, but they do not know his.

sanskrit: ye ke cit sarvalokeṣu daivaṃ pitryaṃ ca kurvate dānāni ca prayacchanti tapyanti ca tapo mahat
english: Whoever in all the worlds perform rites for the gods and for the ancestors, and bestow gifts, and practice great austerity—

sanskrit: sarveṣām āśrayo viṣṇur aiśvaraṃ vidhim āsthitaḥ sarvabhūtakṛtāvāso vāsudeveti cocyate
english: the refuge of them all is Viṣṇu, who abides in lordly ordinance; because he has made his dwelling in all beings, he is called Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: ayaṃ hi nityaḥ paramo maharṣir; mahāvibhūtir guṇavān nirguṇākhyaḥ guṇaiś ca saṃyogam upaiti śīghraṃ; kālo yathartāv ṛtusaṃprayuktaḥ
english: For he is the eternal, supreme Great Seer, of vast might, possessed of qualities yet called free of qualities; he swiftly enters into union with the qualities, as time, in its season, joins itself to the seasons.

sanskrit: naivāsya vindanti gatiṃ mahātmano; na cāgatiṃ kaś cid ihānupasyati jñānātmakāḥ saṃyamino maharṣayaḥ; paśyanti nityaṃ puruṣaṃ guṇādhikam
english: None can find the going of this great-souled one, nor does anyone here perceive his coming. Only the great seers, made of knowledge and self-restrained, behold forever the Puruṣa who transcends the qualities.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca aho hy ekāntinaḥ sarvān prīṇāti bhagavān hariḥ vidhiprayuktāṃ pūjāṃ ca gṛhṇāti bhagavān svayam
english: Janamejaya said: Ah, the Lord Hari gives delight to all the single-minded devotees, and the Lord himself receives the worship offered according to ordinance.

sanskrit: ye tu dagdhendhanā loke puṇyapāpavivarjitāḥ teṣāṃ tvayābhinirdiṣṭā pāraṃparyāgatā gatiḥ
english: But for those in the world whose fuel of karma is burnt away, who are free of merit and demerit, you have set forth the goal that is reached by the unbroken succession of the tradition.

sanskrit: caturthyāṃ caiva te gatyāṃ gacchanti puruṣottamam ekāntinas tu puruṣā gacchanti paramaṃ padam
english: By the fourth course they go to the Supreme Person; the single-minded ones indeed go to the highest abode.

sanskrit: nūnam ekāntadharmo 'yaṃ śreṣṭho nārāyaṇapriyaḥ agatvā gatayas tisro yad gacchanty avyayaṃ harim
english: Surely this dharma of single-minded devotion is the most excellent, dear to Nārāyaṇa, since its followers, without passing through the three other courses, go straight to the imperishable Hari.

sanskrit: sahopaniṣadān vedān ye viprāḥ samyag āsthitāḥ paṭhanti vidhim āsthāya ye cāpi yatidharmiṇaḥ
english: Those brahmins who, abiding rightly, recite the Vedas together with the Upaniṣads, holding fast to ordinance, and those too who follow the dharma of ascetics—

sanskrit: tebhyo viśiṣṭāṃ jānāmi gatim ekāntināṃ nṛṇām kenaiṣa dharmaḥ kathito devena ṛṣiṇāpi vā
english: I know that the goal of the single-minded men is more distinguished than theirs. By whom was this dharma declared—by a god, or by a seer?

sanskrit: ekāntināṃ ca kā caryā kadā cotpāditā vibho etan me saṃśayaṃ chindhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: And what is the practice of the single-minded ones, and when was it brought forth, O mighty one? Cut through this doubt of mine, for great is my curiosity.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca samupoḍheṣv anīkeṣu kurupāṇḍavayor mṛdhe arjune vimanaske ca gītā bhagavatā svayam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the armies of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas had been drawn up for battle, and Arjuna was dispirited, it was sung by the Lord himself.

sanskrit: āgatiś ca gatiś caiva pūrvaṃ te kathitā mayā gahano hy eṣa dharmo vai durvijñeyo 'kṛtātmabhiḥ
english: The coming and the going I have already related to you. For this dharma is profound, hard to comprehend for those who have not perfected the self.

sanskrit: saṃmitaḥ sāmavedena puraivādiyuge kṛtaḥ dhāryate svayam īśena rājan nārāyaṇena ha
english: It is measured by the Sāmaveda, established of old in the first age; it is upheld, O king, by the Lord Nārāyaṇa himself.

sanskrit: etam arthaṃ mahārāja pṛṣṭaḥ pārthena nāradaḥ ṛṣimadhye mahābhāgaḥ śṛṇvatoḥ kṛṣṇabhīṣmayoḥ
english: On this matter, O great king, the highly blessed Nārada, questioned by Pārtha amid the seers, while Kṛṣṇa and Bhīṣma listened—

sanskrit: guruṇā ca mamāpy eṣa kathito nṛpasattama yathā tu kathitas tatra nāradena tathā śṛṇu
english: and this was related by my teacher to me as well, O best of kings. Hear it now just as it was related there by Nārada.

sanskrit: yadāsīn mānasaṃ janma nārāyaṇamukhodgatam brahmaṇaḥ pṛthivīpāla tadā nārāyaṇaḥ svayam tena dharmeṇa kṛtavān daivaṃ pitryaṃ ca bhārata
english: When there was the mind-born birth of Brahmā, sprung from the mouth of Nārāyaṇa, O protector of the earth, then Nārāyaṇa himself, by that dharma, performed the rites for the gods and for the ancestors, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: phenapā ṛṣayaś caiva taṃ dharmaṃ pratipedire vaikhānasāḥ phenapebhyo dharmam etaṃ prapedire vaikhānasebhyaḥ somas tu tataḥ so 'ntardadhe punaḥ
english: The Phenapa seers received that dharma; the Vaikhānasas received this dharma from the Phenapas, and from the Vaikhānasas Soma received it; thereafter that god vanished once more.

sanskrit: yadāsīc cākṣuṣaṃ janma dvitīyaṃ brahmaṇo nṛpa tadā pitāmahāt somād etaṃ dharmam ajānata nārāyaṇātmakaṃ rājan rudrāya pradadau ca saḥ
english: When there was the second birth of Brahmā, the eye-born one, O king, then from the grandsire Soma he came to know this dharma, of Nārāyaṇa's essence, O king, and he gave it over to Rudra.

sanskrit: tato yogasthito rudraḥ purā kṛtayuge nṛpa vālakhilyān ṛṣīn sarvān dharmam etam apāṭhayat antardadhe tato bhūyas tasya devasya māyayā
english: Then Rudra, established in yoga, of old in the Kṛta age, O king, taught this dharma to all the Vālakhilya seers; thereafter it vanished once more by the magic power of that god.

sanskrit: tṛtīyaṃ brahmaṇo janma yadāsīd vācikaṃ mahat tatraiṣa dharmaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ svayaṃ nārāyaṇān nṛpa
english: When there was the third, the great speech-born birth of Brahmā, then this dharma came forth from Nārāyaṇa himself, O king.

sanskrit: suparṇo nāma tam ṛṣiḥ prāptavān puruṣottamāt tapasā vai sutaptena damena niyamena ca
english: The seer named Suparṇa obtained it from the Supreme Person, through austerity well practiced, through self-control and discipline.

sanskrit: triḥ parikrāntavān etat suparṇo dharmam uttamam yasmāt tasmād vrataṃ hy etat trisauparṇam ihocyate
english: Suparṇa traversed this supreme dharma three times over; for that reason this observance is here called the Trisauparṇa.

sanskrit: ṛgvedapāṭhapaṭhitaṃ vratam etad dhi duścaram suparṇāc cāpy adhigato dharma eṣa sanātanaḥ
english: This observance, recited in the recitation of the Ṛgveda, is indeed hard to fulfill; and this eternal dharma was obtained from Suparṇa as well.

sanskrit: vāyunā dvipadāṃ śreṣṭha prathito jagadāyuṣā vāyoḥ sakāśāt prāptaś ca ṛṣibhir vighasāśibhiḥ
english: By Vāyu, O best of bipeds, it was made known—Vāyu, the life-breath of the world; and from the presence of Vāyu it was obtained by the seers who eat the remnants of offerings.

sanskrit: tebhyo mahodadhiś cainaṃ prāptavān dharmam uttamam tataḥ so 'ntardadhe bhūyo nārāyaṇasamāhitaḥ
english: From them the great Ocean obtained this supreme dharma; thereafter it vanished once more, gathered back into Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: yadā bhūyaḥ śravaṇajā sṛṣṭir āsīn mahātmanaḥ brahmaṇaḥ puruṣavyāghra tatra kīrtayataḥ śṛṇu
english: When once again there was the ear-born creation of the great-souled Brahmā, O tiger among men, listen as I relate it.

sanskrit: jagat sraṣṭumanā devo harir nārāyaṇaḥ svayam cintayām āsa puruṣaṃ jagatsargakaraṃ prabhuḥ
english: The god Hari Nārāyaṇa himself, intent on creating the world, the Lord, brought to mind a Person who would make the creation of the world.

sanskrit: atha cintayatas tasya karṇābhyāṃ puruṣaḥ sṛtaḥ prajāsargakaro brahmā tam uvāca jagatpatiḥ
english: Then, as he was pondering, a Person issued from his two ears—Brahmā, the maker of creatures' generation; and the Lord of the world addressed him:

sanskrit: sṛja prajāḥ putra sarvā mukhataḥ pādatas tathā śreyas tava vidhāsyāmi balaṃ tejaś ca suvrata
english: "Create all the creatures, my son, from the mouth and likewise from the feet; I shall ordain your welfare, your strength and your splendor, O you of good vows."

sanskrit: dharmaṃ ca matto gṛhṇīṣva sātvataṃ nāma nāmataḥ tena sarvaṃ kṛtayugaṃ sthāpayasva yathāvidhi
english: "And receive from me the dharma named Sātvata by name; by it, establish the whole Kṛta age according to ordinance."

sanskrit: tato brahmā namaścakre devāya harimedhase dharmaṃ cāgryaṃ sa jagrāha sarahasyaṃ sasaṃgraham āraṇyakena sahitaṃ nārāyaṇamukhodgatam
english: Then Brahmā made obeisance to the god Harimedhas, and he took up the foremost dharma, together with its mystery and its summary, accompanied by the Āraṇyaka, sprung from the mouth of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: upadiśya tato dharmaṃ brahmaṇe 'mitatejase taṃ kārtayugadharmāṇaṃ nirāśīḥkarmasaṃjñitam jagāma tamasaḥ pāraṃ yatrāvyaktaṃ vyavasthitam
english: Having then imparted to Brahmā of measureless splendor that dharma proper to the Kṛta age, known as action free of desire, he went beyond the darkness, where the Unmanifest abides.

sanskrit: tato 'tha varado devo brahmalokapitāmahaḥ asṛjat sa tadā lokān kṛtsnān sthāvarajaṅgamān
english: Then the boon-granting god, the grandsire of the world of Brahmā, created at that time all the worlds entire, the unmoving and the moving.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāvartata tadā ādau kṛtayugaṃ śubham tato hi sātvato dharmo vyāpya lokān avasthitaḥ
english: Then at the beginning the auspicious Kṛta age set in; and thereupon the Sātvata dharma, pervading the worlds, stood established.

sanskrit: tenaivādyena dharmeṇa brahmā lokavisargakṛt pūjayām āsa deveśaṃ hariṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum
english: By that very first dharma, Brahmā, the maker of the worlds' outpouring, worshipped the Lord of gods, Hari Nārāyaṇa, the Master.

sanskrit: dharmapratiṣṭhāhetoś ca manuṃ svārociṣaṃ tataḥ adhyāpayām āsa tadā lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: And for the sake of establishing dharma, he then taught it to Manu Svārociṣa, out of his desire for the welfare of the worlds.

sanskrit: tataḥ svārociṣaḥ putraṃ svayaṃ śaṅkhapadaṃ nṛpa adhyāpayat purāvyagraḥ sarvalokapatir vibhuḥ
english: Then Svārociṣa, undistracted of old, the lord and master of all worlds, himself taught it to his son Śaṅkhapada, O king.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaṅkhapadaś cāpi putram ātmajam aurasam diśāpālaṃ sudharmāṇam adhyāpayata bhārata tataḥ so 'ntardadhe bhūyaḥ prāpte tretāyuge punaḥ
english: Then Śaṅkhapada too taught it to his own son, born of his body, Sudharman the guardian of a quarter, O Bhārata; thereafter it vanished once more, when the Tretā age had come again.

sanskrit: nāsikyajanmani purā brahmaṇaḥ pārthivottama dharmam etaṃ svayaṃ devo harir nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ ujjagārāravindākṣo brahmaṇaḥ paśyatas tadā
english: At the nostril-born birth of Brahmā of old, O best of kings, the god Hari Nārāyaṇa himself, the lotus-eyed Lord, brought forth this dharma while Brahmā looked on.

sanskrit: sanatkumāro bhagavāṃs tataḥ prādhītavān nṛpa sanatkumārād api ca vīraṇo vai prajāpatiḥ kṛtādau kuruśārdūla dharmam etam adhītavān
english: Then the blessed Sanatkumāra learned it, O king; and from Sanatkumāra the lord of creatures Vīraṇa, at the dawn of the Kṛta age, O tiger of the Kurus, learned this dharma.

sanskrit: vīraṇaś cāpy adhītyainaṃ raucyāya manave dadau raucyaḥ putrāya śuddhāya suvratāya sumedhase
english: And Vīraṇa, having studied it, gave it to Manu Raucya; Raucya gave it to his son, the pure, devout, and wise Suvrata—

sanskrit: kukṣināmne 'tha pradadau diśāṃ pālāya dharmiṇe tataḥ so 'ntardadhe bhūyo nārāyaṇamukhodgataḥ
english: that is, he bestowed it upon the righteous guardian of the quarters named Kukṣi; thereafter it vanished once more, the dharma sprung from the mouth of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: aṇḍaje janmani punar brahmaṇe hariyonaye eṣa dharmaḥ samudbhūto nārāyaṇamukhāt punaḥ
english: At the egg-born birth, again, of Brahmā whose source is Hari, this dharma arose once more from the mouth of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: gṛhīto brahmaṇā rājan prayuktaś ca yathāvidhi adhyāpitāś ca munayo nāmnā barhiṣado nṛpa
english: It was received by Brahmā, O king, and applied according to ordinance; and the sages named the Barhiṣads were instructed in it, O king.

sanskrit: barhiṣadbhyaś ca saṃkrāntaḥ sāmavedāntagaṃ dvijam jyeṣṭhaṃ nāmnābhivikhyātaṃ jyeṣṭhasāmavrato hariḥ
english: And from the Barhiṣads, Hari—keeper of the observance of the eldest Sāman—passed it on to the twice-born one who had reached the end of the Sāmaveda, renowned by the name Jyeṣṭha.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhāc cāpy anusaṃkrānto rājānam avikampanam antardadhe tato rājann eṣa dharmaḥ prabhor hareḥ
english: And from Jyeṣṭha it passed on to King Avikampana; thereafter, O king, this dharma of the Lord Hari vanished away.

sanskrit: yad idaṃ saptamaṃ janma padmajaṃ brahmaṇo nṛpa tatraiṣa dharmaḥ kathitaḥ svayaṃ nārāyaṇena hi
english: This which is the seventh birth of Brahmā, the lotus-born, O king—there this dharma was declared by Nārāyaṇa himself.

sanskrit: pitāmahāya śuddhāya yugādau lokadhāriṇe pitāmahaś ca dakṣāya dharmam etaṃ purā dadau
english: To the pure grandsire, the upholder of the worlds at the age's dawn, and the grandsire gave this dharma of old to Dakṣa.

sanskrit: tato jyeṣṭhe tu dauhitre prādād dakṣo nṛpottama āditye savitur jyeṣṭhe vivasvāñ jagṛhe tataḥ
english: Then Dakṣa bestowed it upon his eldest grandson, O best of kings; and from him Vivasvat received it, the eldest son of Savitṛ among the Ādityas.

sanskrit: tretāyugādau ca punar vivasvān manave dadau manuś ca lokabhūtyarthaṃ sutāyekṣvākave dadau
english: And at the dawn of the Tretā age, again, Vivasvat gave it to Manu; and Manu, for the welfare of the worlds, gave it to his son Ikṣvāku.

sanskrit: ikṣvākuṇā ca kathito vyāpya lokān avasthitaḥ gamiṣyati kṣayānte ca punar nārāyaṇaṃ nṛpa
english: And declared by Ikṣvāku, it stood pervading the worlds; and at the end of the cosmic dissolution it shall go back again to Nārāyaṇa, O king.

sanskrit: vratināṃ cāpi yo dharmaḥ sa te pūrvaṃ nṛpottama kathito harigītāsu samāsavidhikalpitaḥ
english: And the dharma which belongs to those who keep the vows, that, O best of kings, was related to you before in the Songs of Hari, set forth in summary form.

sanskrit: nāradena tu saṃprāptaḥ sarahasyaḥ sasaṃgrahaḥ eṣa dharmo jagannāthāt sākṣān nārāyaṇān nṛpa
english: By Nārada this dharma was obtained, with its mystery and its summary, directly from the Lord of the world, from Nārāyaṇa, O king.

sanskrit: evam eṣa mahān dharma ādyo rājan sanātanaḥ durvijñeyo duṣkaraś ca sātvatair dhāryate sadā
english: Thus this great dharma, primordial and eternal, O king, hard to comprehend and hard to practice, is upheld at all times by the Sātvatas.

sanskrit: dharmajñānena caitena suprayuktena karmaṇā ahiṃsādharmayuktena prīyate harir īśvaraḥ
english: By this knowledge of dharma, and by action well applied and joined with the dharma of non-injury, the Lord Hari is well pleased.

sanskrit: ekavyūhavibhāgo vā kva cid dvivyūhasaṃjñitaḥ trivyūhaś cāpi saṃkhyātaś caturvyūhaś ca dṛśyate
english: In one place his distribution is of a single array; somewhere it is called a twofold array; he is reckoned as a threefold array, and a fourfold array too is seen.

sanskrit: harir eva hi kṣetrajño nirmamo niṣkalas tathā jīvaś ca sarvabhūteṣu pañcabhūtaguṇātigaḥ
english: For Hari alone is the Knower of the field, free of self-claiming and without parts, and the living soul in all beings, transcending the qualities of the five elements.

sanskrit: manaś ca prathitaṃ rājan pañcendriyasamīraṇam eṣa lokanidhir dhīmān eṣa lokavisargakṛt
english: He is the renowned mind too, O king, that sets the five senses in motion; he is the wise treasure-house of the worlds, he is the maker of the worlds' outpouring.

sanskrit: akartā caiva kartā ca kāryaṃ kāraṇam eva ca yathecchati tathā rājan krīḍate puruṣo 'vyayaḥ
english: He is both the non-doer and the doer, the effect and the cause as well; just as he wishes, O king, so does the imperishable Person play.

sanskrit: eṣa ekāntidharmas te kīrtito nṛpasattama mayā guruprasādena durvijñeyo 'kṛtātmabhiḥ ekāntino hi puruṣā durlabhā bahavo nṛpa
english: This dharma of single-minded devotion has been recounted to you, O best of kings, by me through the grace of my teacher—hard to comprehend for those who have not perfected the self; for single-minded men, O king, are not to be found in great numbers.

sanskrit: yady ekāntibhir ākīrṇaṃ jagat syāt kurunandana ahiṃsakair ātmavidbhiḥ sarvabhūtahite rataiḥ bhavet kṛtayugaprāptir āśīḥkarmavivarjitaiḥ
english: If the world were thronged with the single-minded, O joy of the Kurus—men who do no harm, who know the Self, who delight in the welfare of all beings and have renounced action done with desire—then the Kṛta age would be regained.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa bhagavān vyāso gurur mama viśāṃ pate kathayām āsa dharmajño dharmarājñe dvijottamaḥ
english: Thus did the blessed Vyāsa, my teacher, O lord of peoples, the knower of dharma, the best of the twice-born, relate it to the Dharma King.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇāṃ saṃnidhau rājañ śṛṇvatoḥ kṛṣṇabhīṣmayoḥ tasyāpy akathayat pūrvaṃ nāradaḥ sumahātapāḥ
english: In the presence of the seers, O king, while Kṛṣṇa and Bhīṣma listened—and to him too, before, Nārada of mighty austerity had related it—

sanskrit: devaṃ paramakaṃ brahma śvetaṃ candrābham acyutam yatra caikāntino yānti nārāyaṇaparāyaṇāḥ
english: the supreme god, the highest Brahman, white, with the luster of the moon, the unfallen, to whom the single-minded ones go, wholly devoted to Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ dharmaṃ pratibuddhair niṣevitam na kurvanti kathaṃ viprā anye nānāvrate sthitāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: This dharma of many kinds, practiced by the awakened—why do other brahmins, established in their various observances, not follow it?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tisraḥ prakṛtayo rājan dehabandheṣu nirmitāḥ sāttvikī rājasī caiva tāmasī ceti bhārata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Three natures, O king, are fashioned within the bonds of the body—the sāttvika, the rājasa, and the tāmasa, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: dehabandheṣu puruṣaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ kurukulodvaha sāttvikaḥ puruṣavyāghra bhaven mokṣārthaniścitaḥ
english: Among those bound in the body, the best of men, O upholder of the Kuru line, is the sāttvika one, O tiger among men—he it is who would be resolved upon the goal of liberation.

sanskrit: atrāpi sa vijānāti puruṣaṃ brahmavartinam nārāyaṇaparo mokṣas tato vai sāttvikaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: And here too he discerns the Person abiding in Brahman; since liberation has Nārāyaṇa for its highest ground, the sāttvika one is verily so esteemed.

sanskrit: manīṣitaṃ ca prāpnoti cintayan puruṣottamam ekāntabhaktiḥ satataṃ nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ
english: And he attains the object of his heart's desire, meditating on the Supreme Person—single-minded in devotion forever, wholly given over to Nārāyaṇa.
